_comment: Prompt fragments for gmail_parser.js. The MAIN extraction system prompt lives in leedz_config.json (gmailParser.systemPrompt - also JSON, edit it there); this file holds the runtime fragments assembled around it. All prose here was moved verbatim out of gmail_parser.js (standing rule: prompts are never hardcoded in JS).

assembly._comment: Top-level layout of the full extraction prompt. Placeholders: {systemPrompt} (from leedz_config.json with dates filled), {sellerIdentity} (block below, or empty), {headerMetadata} (block below), {content} (email thread text).
lines: {systemPrompt}
{sellerIdentity}
{headerMetadata}
Email Thread Content:
{content}

headerMetadata._comment: Header identity + client-identity rules. Placeholders: {headerName} {headerEmail} {weakNote} (weakInboxNote below when the header looks like a shared inbox, else empty). The 2026-07-22 fix: header identity is METADATA, not ground truth - the real client is usually in the signature block.
lines: EMAIL HEADER METADATA (may be a shared mailbox — verify against the message text):
Header Name: {headerName}
Header Email: {headerEmail}
{weakNote}
CLIENT IDENTITY RULES:
1. The client is the PERSON who wrote the inquiry — prefer the signature block (name / title / direct phone) over the mailbox display name.
2. Only return an email address that literally appears in the headers or message text.
3. Extract the client's phone from the signature when present.

weakInboxNote._comment: Injected into headerMetadata {weakNote} only when Client._identityWeak is set (shared/generic inbox detected).
lines: NOTE: the header identity above looks like a SHARED/GENERIC inbox, not a person. Find the actual PERSON who wrote the message — check the signature block for their name, title, and direct phone, and return THAT as the client name/phone.

inboxDemandNote._comment: INBOX CATCHER (2026-08-14, PRECRIME build item #4). Injected into headerMetadata {weakNote} when the sender is a PLATFORM NOTIFICATION domain (facebookmail, Nextdoor, Google Alerts, Craigslist) — see gmail_parser PLATFORM_NOTIFICATION_DOMAINS. The email relays someone ELSE'S post; the poster is the client, the post is the demand.
lines: NOTE: this email is a PLATFORM NOTIFICATION (a Facebook group post, Nextdoor digest, Google Alert, or Craigslist alert) relaying SOMEONE ELSE'S post or listing. The platform is NEVER the client.
- The Client is the PERSON WHO WROTE THE POST: take their name from the post byline (e.g. "Jane Smith posted in Westside Weddings"). A name-only client is fine.

- Some notifications show NO poster name (the byline is just the group name). Then leave the client name EMPTY — never use the group or platform as the name. STILL extract the Booking (the ask, occasion, location) and quote the ask in clientNotes; the post link carries the poster's identity and research follows it.
- Return an email/phone for them ONLY if it appears verbatim inside the post text. NEVER return the platform's address.
- The post text is a DEMAND SIGNAL: extract the event they are asking about (occasion, date, venue/city) into the Booking, and quote their ask verbatim in clientNotes.

sellerIdentity._comment: Never-extract-the-seller-as-client block, built from STATE.BusinessIdentity (VALUE_PROP). Placeholders: {sellerName} {companyName} {emails} {phones}. Empty string is used when identity is unavailable (IdentityFilter still removes the seller procedurally).
lines: SELLER IDENTITY (NEVER extract these as the client - they are the seller/user, appearing in From: headers and quoted "On ... wrote:" reply markers):
- Name: {sellerName}
- Company: {companyName}
- Emails: {emails}
- Phones: {phones}

repair._comment: One-pass correction prompt run when DateEvidence source-verification rejects extracted date/time fields. Placeholders: {fields} (comma list, e.g. Booking.startTime), {currentYear}, {content} (email thread text). OUTPUT CONTRACT: a FLAT object keyed by the exact field paths in {fields}, values only - e.g. {"Booking.endTime": "10:00 PM"}. Deliberately does NOT echo the whole extraction back: re-emitting long description strings made the model produce unescaped quotes and the JSON failed to parse (2026-08-11). The caller merges these values onto the first-pass result and RE-VERIFIES them, so a wrong answer here is still caught.
lines: You previously extracted booking fields from a Gmail thread. These fields could not be verified against the email text: {fields}.
Re-examine the email and report ONLY those fields.
RULES:
1. Re-extract the listed fields ONLY from text literally present in the email body.
2. If a field is not literally present, return null for that field.
3. DO NOT GUESS. DO NOT INFER AM/PM. DO NOT HALLUCINATE TIMES OR DATES.
4. startDate/endDate are ISO YYYY-MM-DD; if the email has no year use {currentYear}; never roll a no-year date into next year.
5. Times are 12-hour with AM/PM (e.g. "7:00 PM"); return null if no time with AM/PM context is literally present.
OUTPUT: a single flat JSON object whose keys are EXACTLY the field paths listed above, and nothing else. Example shape:
{"Booking.endTime": "10:00 PM", "Booking.startDate": null}
Do NOT return any other field. Do NOT repeat the email. Do NOT add commentary or markdown fences.
Email thread:
{content}

fallbackSystemPrompt._comment: Used ONLY if leedz_config.json gmailParser.systemPrompt is missing.
lines: Extract booking information from the following email thread and output JSON.
